outcomes: Each crate of a Cargo workspace is a Putnami project named by its package, with an edge to each crate it depends on by path, and the stack root of the Cargo workspace that holds it
putnami lint, test and build run the Rust profile's cargo steps in each crate's directory, and a second run over an unchanged tree is a cache hit
The test task reads the nextest JUnit report and the cargo-llvm-cov LCOV report into the test and coverage summary, with each case and each coverage line attributed to its crate
Each task reads only the inputs it needs: lint does not rerun on a lockfile or nextest configuration change, and build does not rerun on a test change
A crate overrides any value of the Rust profile in its putnami.json, and the override reaches the cache key

On the Cargo detector's fixture repository, with the real cargo, cargo-nextest and cargo-llvm-cov, lint, test and build pass with no putnami.json override and every case and coverage line attributed; a CI leg that installs those tools proves it, since the workspace gate has none

On a machine with no Rust, cargo-nextest or cargo-llvm-cov, putnami lint, test and build install what is missing and pass on a Cargo repository; a machine that holds a Rust satisfying the repository's statement keeps it

putnami run and serve start a binary crate, and putnami package and publish ship it as archives, an OCI image built from any host with no docker daemon, or a crate on a registry at the Putnami release version

putnami install fetches the crates each stack root's Cargo.lock names, a hosted run downloads them with workspace-fetch and runs every cargo step offline, deps-upgrade refreshes each Cargo.lock, lint checks the documentation links, and putnami test -t runs the tests whose name holds the filter
nonGoals: A C linker, which rustc needs and the machine must hold, and the targets and components a rust-toolchain file lists beyond rustfmt, clippy and llvm-tools
A member of a nested Cargo workspace whose root package depends on that member: the edge to its root would close a cycle
A release-set member: publish --channel does not carry a crate, an image or an archive of a Rust project

Major version bumps: cargo update --breaking is unstable in the cargo of Rust 1.99.1, the release the extension installs by default, and cargo-edit's cargo upgrade is not installed, so deps-upgrade stays within each semver requirement

An offline task that runs a Rust, cargo-nextest or cargo-llvm-cov installed under the Putnami home: the stack core installs and selects them only with the network, so a hosted run runs the ones on its runner's PATH
Handing the read credential of a hosted run to cargo: its hosts serve no Cargo registry, and cargo authenticates to an alternative registry with its own credential providers

requirements.text: The probe answers, for each directory the observe Cargo detector knows as a crate: its package name, the directories of the crates it depends on by path, the extension @putnami/rust, the tag rust, and metadata naming the crate, its stack root and the expected toolchain version. The stack root is the workspace root for a member of the root Cargo workspace, the nearest enclosing directory whose [workspace] names it as a member, else its own directory.

A virtual Cargo workspace below the workspace root is an input-only project: metadata naming its root and no crate, tasks that run no step, and a rust:<task> selector that answers the stack-root files of that task in its directory. Each crate of a nested workspace depends on the project at its stack root, so a change to the root's Cargo.lock reruns its crates' test and build and not their lint. A crate the root package depends on gets no such edge and is left out with stacks.stack_root_unsupported.

Each task first compares rustc --version with the version rust-toolchain.toml or rust-toolchain states, in the crate then at its stack root: a mismatch fails with stacks.toolchain_mismatch unless toolchain.check is warn, a missing rustc with stacks.toolchain_missing. It then runs each profile step in the crate's directory with no shell, one task at a time per stack root; a step that exits non-zero fails with stacks.step_failed.

After its steps, the test task copies the JUnit reports the profile names into its output directory and reads them, with the LCOV report, through the evidence readers into the test and coverage summary. A failed case fails the task with stacks.test_failed; a JUnit or coverage pattern that matches no report fails it with stacks.report_missing.

Each JUnit case of the test task is attributed by its nextest binary id, its class name else its suite name (pricing::integration, api::bin/api), to the crate of that package, with - and _ read as one. A case of another crate is left out of the summary; a case whose id names no crate is counted and reported with the warning stacks.test_unattributed.

Each file of a coverage report, an absolute path as cargo-llvm-cov writes it or a path relative to the crate, is attributed to the crate whose directory holds it, the deepest one. The lines of another crate's file are left out of the summary; the lines of a file in no crate are left out and reported with the warning stacks.coverage_unmapped.

lint reads the crate's sources, its test, bench and example targets, the Cargo manifests and configuration, and the rustfmt and clippy configurations; test reads the sources, targets, manifests, nextest configuration and lockfiles; build reads the sources, manifests and lockfiles. After its steps, build copies the stack root's target/debug/<crate> binary into its output when cargo wrote one.

options["@putnami/rust"] in a crate's own putnami.json overrides the profile: an object merges, any other value replaces the profile's whole. The steps run and the files the rust:<task> selectors answer follow the resolved profile, and putnami.json is an input of every task. An unknown member, a change to id or markers, or a stack-root input the manifest does not declare fails the task with stacks.project_config_invalid.

The manifest passes the stack core's conformance kit: its markers are the profile's, it lists the rust:lint, rust:test and rust:build selectors, and each command runs one task that depends on the same task upstream, reads its selector and the profile's stack-root files for that task, and declares its command-output reports directory.

A task whose rustc is missing, or outside the version a rust-toolchain file states, installs that version, or the extension's default, with the rustup the extension pins by SHA-256, in a rustup home under the Putnami home, once per version. A rustc on PATH that satisfies the statement runs and nothing is installed. An offline run installs nothing and reports stacks.toolchain_missing.

The test task, and no other task of the profile, makes cargo-nextest and cargo-llvm-cov available when the PATH holds neither: each is installed from an archive the extension pins by SHA-256 and its directory is appended to the PATH of the task, so a tool the machine holds comes first. workspace-install installs the same archives ahead of the first test.
A test task on a Rust with no llvm-tools runs cargo nextest with its JUnit report only, reads no LCOV report, and reports the warning stacks.coverage_unavailable.
A crate with src/main.rs, a src/bin target or a [[bin]] table is a project of type application; any other crate is a library, and run and serve skip a library.

putnami run runs cargo run --package <crate> --locked once after the toolchain check, with no cache and no stack-root lock. The words of --args reach the program, --port sets PORT, and the task returns the program's exit code as its exit-code result; a non-zero exit fails the task.

putnami serve runs the same command until the user stops it, with no stack-root lock, PORT set from --port, 3000 by default and a free port for 0, and announces the server ready once the port accepts connections. A program that exits on its own fails the task with its exit code.

package compiles the crate's binary in release mode with cargo zigbuild for the platforms its channels need: --platform for docker, linux/amd64 by default, and --platforms for archives, the five archive platforms by default. A Linux binary links against glibc 2.36, the libc of the image base, and a library crate compiles nothing.

The compile step uses the Rust the extension installs, adds each rustup target it needs, and installs cargo-zigbuild and zig under the Putnami home, whatever the PATH holds, each pinned by version and SHA-256 per platform. An offline run installs nothing and fails naming what is missing.
package --archives writes <artifact>-<platform>.tar.gz per platform with the binary at the archive root, and the publication manifest @putnami/cloud uploads from.

package --docker assembles a reproducible OCI layout for one Linux platform with no docker daemon: the binary on a digest-pinned cc-debian12 base, PORT set from --port, and the manifest the shared Docker publisher reads.

package --crates copies the stack root without its build output and writes the release version into each manifest and each normal path dependency, leaving the checkout untouched. publish --crates runs cargo publish from that copy, dependencies first; a version the registry already holds is reused, and --dry-run uploads nothing.
publish --docker pushes the assembled image through the shared Docker publisher, and the crates and docker publish tasks each declare their channel with the registry effect.

workspace-fetch reads and closes the credential descriptor of a hosted run before it starts any process, and uses nothing it held. At each stack root that holds a Cargo.lock it runs cargo fetch --locked with RUSTC_WRAPPER and RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER empty and RUSTC set to the selected rustc: no build script, procedural macro, wrapper or compiler the repository names runs, and the repository is not written. A root with no Cargo.lock is left out with the warning rust.lockfile_missing, which names it.

When PUTNAMI_OFFLINE_DEPENDENCIES is 1, every job of the runtime but publish-crates sets CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true before it starts a process, so each cargo of lint, test, build, run, serve, package and workspace-install reads only the crates workspace-fetch downloaded. No job sets CARGO_HOME: workspace-fetch and the tasks read the cargo home of the environment.

workspace-install runs cargo fetch, which writes a missing Cargo.lock, at each stack root of the workspace's projects, except a project disable.tags excludes and a root where cargo fetch --locked --offline passes, unless the force flag is set; then it installs cargo-nextest and cargo-llvm-cov when the PATH holds neither. Offline, it runs cargo fetch --locked --offline at each root that holds a Cargo.lock, writes and installs nothing, and leaves a root with no Cargo.lock out with rust.lockfile_missing.

deps-upgrade runs cargo update at each stack root of the workspace's projects, with the cargo the toolchain check selects: each locked version moves to the newest one its semver requirement accepts, as bundle update, composer update, pub upgrade and swift package update do. With offline dependencies it fails with rust.cargo_update_failed, which says that cargo update needs the network, and runs no cargo.

lint checks every relative link and anchor of the project's README.md files and doc/ trees with the SDK's documentation link check, and a broken one fails lint. The docs-links flag, on by default, turns the check off. A crate below the project, marked by its Cargo.toml, answers for its own documents.

test with the test flag, short -t, passes its value to nextest as -E 'test(~<value>)', with the characters a name matcher reads only escaped, with or without coverage, so it selects the tests whose name contains the value. It adds --no-tests=pass when cargo nextest run --help lists --no-tests, so a crate in which the filter selects no test passes. A last step that runs no nextest gets no argument. The value is part of the task's key, so a filtered result never answers an unfiltered run.
